record.paper_title: Finite translation generalized quadrangles: old results, new results, open problems
record.original_question: Let O(n, n, q) be a pseudo-oval, meaning a set of q^n + 1 mutually constrained (n − 1)-dimensional subspaces in PG(3n − 1, q) as defined in the paper. Is every such pseudo-oval regular, in the sense of arising from the paper’s field-extension construction of a regular pseudo-oval?

evidence.quote: 1. Is any O(n, n, q) regular?
For n = m such a set O(n, n, q) is called a pseudo-oval or a generalized oval or an [n − 1]-oval of PG(3n − 1, q).
Here, we speak of a regular pseudo-oval, respectively a regular pseudo-ovoid.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the finite projective space $\mathrm{PG}(3n-1,q)$ over the field $\mathbb{F}_q$, where $n\geq 1$ and $q$ is a prime power. A pseudo-oval (also called a generalized oval, or $[n-1]$-oval) is a set
$$\mathcal{O} = \{\pi_0, \pi_1, \ldots, \pi_{q^n}\}$$
of $q^n+1$ pairwise disjoint $(n-1)$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathrm{PG}(3n-1,q)$ satisfying the tangent-space condition: every three distinct elements of $\mathcal{O}$ span a $(3n-1)$-dimensional subspace (equivalently, they are in general position), and for each $\pi_i\in\mathcal{O}$ there exists a $(2n-1)$-dimensional subspace $T_i$ (the tangent space at $\pi_i$) containing $\pi_i$ and meeting every $\pi_j$, $j\neq i$, trivially.

The standard field-extension construction produces a so-called regular pseudo-oval as follows. Let $\mathcal{O}'$ be an oval (a set of $q^n+1$ points, no three collinear) in $\mathrm{PG}(2,q^n)$. Viewing $\mathrm{PG}(2,q^n)$ as $\mathrm{PG}(3n-1,q)$ by restriction of scalars from $\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ to $\mathbb{F}_q$, each point of $\mathcal{O}'$ becomes an $(n-1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_q$-subspace, and the resulting collection is a pseudo-oval in $\mathrm{PG}(3n-1,q)$. A pseudo-oval is called regular if it is projectively equivalent to one obtained in this way.

Question: Is every pseudo-oval in $\mathrm{PG}(3n-1,q)$ regular?
artifact.status_search_result: The general regularity question for pseudo-ovals appears still open. Recent classification work (2024) addresses only small parameters: all pseudo-ovals in $\mathrm{PG}(3n-1,2)$ for $n=3,4$, and in $\mathrm{PG}(3n-1,q)$ for $n=5,6$ under a Desarguesian-plane hypothesis, have been classified, and all known pseudo-ovals are regular, but no general proof or counterexample is reported.

status_evidence.title: Classifying pseudo-ovals, translation generalized quadrangles, and elation Laguerre planes of small order
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of all pseudo-ovals in PG(3n-1,2) for n=3,4, and pseudo-ovals in PG(3n-1,q) for n=5,6 such that one of the associated projective planes is Desarguesian.
status_evidence.claim: Recent partial classifications of pseudo-ovals of small order are known; the general regularity question remains a target.

status_evidence.title: Generalized Ovals: Advanced Concepts
status_evidence.snippet: For m=n, any known [n-1]-oval is regular.
status_evidence.claim: Every known pseudo-oval is regular, but a general proof is not stated.

status_evidence.title: On eggs and translation generalised quadrangles
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of eggs and pseudo-ovals discussing regularity questions
status_evidence.claim: The classification/regularity of pseudo-ovals is an active research topic.
